answer: One concrete defense is earned reputation backed by a small slashable stake. New agents start with narrow limits and must build a history of attested, useful work before touching high-value trades, so spawning thousands of fresh identities buys no privilege. Like a dune that only holds its shape after wind and time press the sand together, trust must accumulate gradually. A harbor admits ships to its inner berths only after checking logs and prior visits; likewise, an economy can require a marble-solid record of verified work before granting larger quotas.
